capabilities: Bridge current file, selection and editor state to Claude Code, Codex CLI, MCP and DeepSeek Harness agents
Provide a selection assistant and inline ghost-text completion through configurable API providers
Run real system terminals and sequential mv-run command lists inside Obsidian
Supply a standalone Vim engine with modes, motions, registers, macros, Ex commands and vault-level .vimrc
Manage the vault's Git repository with staging, diff views and three-way conflict editing
extras: Maintenance note says frequent DeepSeek Harness breaking updates may break mv-agent compatibility; API keys are stored in plaintext in data.json; full manuals (Chinese and English), platform matrices and troubleshooting live outside the README; the Web Viewer context-menu injection is labeled experimental.
motivation: The author built it so agents stay aware of what the user is reading and editing instead of working detached from the live context, and so AI, source code, terminal, Vim and desktop file workflows share one interface.
problem: Obsidian gives coding agents no live view of the current file, selection or terminal output, and offers no built-in terminal, Vim engine, non-Markdown source tooling or Git frontend.
